speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned waking up frightened; can you describe exactly what you see or hear during these episodes, and do your parents notice any specific movements you make while asleep?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. To differentiate between night terrors and nightmares, can you tell me if these frightening episodes happen in the first half of the night or later? Additionally, does she appear to be sweating or breathing heavily during these events, and has anyone seen her thrashing or running around while asleep?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Night Terrors (Sleep Terrors)

The patient's description of yelling and crying with temporary post-episode tiredness, combined with the lack of recollection of bad dreams mentioned in the latest input, is highly suggestive of night terrors rather than nightmares. While she mentioned "recollection," the classic presentation involves no memory of the event, which occurs during the NREM sleep stage; please confirm if she truly has no memory of the frightening episodes themselves and ask her parents to note if she is fully alert during the event. REQUEST IMAGES: Sleep_study_video.
